Post-streptococcal autoimmune basal ganglia disorder; associated rheumatic carditis is separate and occasional in the supplied annotations.

Defined by renal magnesium wasting, hypomagnesemia, nephrocalcinosis and severe retinal abnormalities; recurrent urinary infections are secondary infections.
Congenital anomalous connection of the inferior vena cava to the left-sided atrium.
Retinal degeneration is shared by the Bardet-Biedl and retinitis pigmentosa subtypes; other organ abnormalities are not established across this umbrella.
Autoimmune inflammatory skeletal myopathy; accompanying autoimmune diseases are separately diagnosed, and cardiac involvement is reported only in some patients.
Brain malformations, seizures and profound developmental impairment define disease; fixed contractures in 2/2 and optic atrophy in 1/2 support additional axes.

Congenital fistula of the oral commissure lined by labial mucosa; susceptibility to infection is only a risk.
Hydatid cysts occupy and damage liver in approximately 60-70%; pulmonary cysts occur in roughly 20-30%, insufficiently consistently above the threshold.
Cerebellar degeneration and sensory neuropathy; nystagmus and diplopia reflect neurologic dysfunction without established intrinsic eye damage.
The defining lesions arise in and expand bone; no additional organ involvement is established.
Ataxia, developmental impairment, scoliosis and foot deformities define syndrome; optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Hyperextensible skin alone does not establish injury.
Congenital skeletal muscle weakness with fingerprint inclusions in muscle fibers; nonspecific homeostasis annotation does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Direct injury or dysfunction of the common peroneal nerve or its branches causes motor and sensory deficits.
Umbrella of mosaic nerve sheath tumour syndromes; cutaneous, auditory and other organ manifestations vary substantially by subtype.
Defining association of hypomyelinating leukodystrophy, abnormal dentition or hypodontia, and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
Alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation defect causes muscular dystrophy; developmental brain or cognitive impairment is common (>30%); ocular defects vary with severe subtypes.
Definition localizes the pathological process to the larynx and vocal cords, which belong to the airway axis.
Recurrent immune-mediated eosinophilic inflammation of skin follicles; associated HIV or immunosuppression is a separate condition.
Hereditary amyloid proteopathy; nerve amyloid 4/4, gastrointestinal disease with diarrhea 3/3, cardiac amyloid 1/1. Hepatic amyloid 1/1 omitted under cap; functional impact unclear.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation defect with epileptic neurodegeneration; hepatic metal or glycogen accumulation lacks demonstrated functional damage.
Skeletal dysplasia with contractures defines disease; hearing impairment occurs in 6/9 and intellectual disability in 10/30. Absent sinuses alone do not establish airway damage.
Familial infantile myeloid leukemia-like disorder affecting blood and marrow; no additional common organ damage is established.
